task.prompt:
Write one Oracle stored procedure named sp with exactly this signature: sp(arg1 IN NUMBER, arg2 IN VARCHAR2, arg3 IN VARCHAR2, arg4 IN NUMBER, arg5 IN VARCHAR2, arg6 IN NUMBER). Args by position: restaurant ID, restaurant-name LIKE pattern, restaurant address, student ID, student last name, restaurant-type ID. The attached examples.md shows the call form; use it as a check.

Set threshold := rounded arg1, status text := arg2, row_count := 0, batch_size := 10. Do not commit or rollback, and let any database error propagate.

Pick one threshold case, in order. Below 3, scan restaurants where ID < arg1 and name LIKE arg2. For each read row, if ID > 25 set name to 'PROMOTED'. Else if address = arg3, count visits to that restaurant by students with last name = arg5; when count > 0 set address to 'RETAINED', otherwise delete the restaurant by read ID/name, then its visits, then its restaurant-type assignments. Otherwise set address to 'PENDING', then rating to arg6.

Below 8, scan students with ID between arg4 - 5 and arg4 + 15 inclusive, using read ID/last name. Set major to 700 if read last name = arg5; then if read last name begins 'ACTIVE' set last name to 'PROCESSED', else if read ID > arg4 + 5 add read ID to threshold, else delete the student only for read last name 'EXPIRED'.

Below 18, scan restaurant types with ID > arg6 - 20. Set status text from read type ID: 'LOW_PRIORITY' below 50, 'MEDIUM_PRIORITY' below 150, otherwise 'HIGH_PRIORITY'. Then add 10 to that type ID, then add 10 to restaurant-type assignments whose type ID was the read value.

Below 25, set address = 'ARCHIVED' for restaurants with ID < arg1 and name <> arg2, then stop with the normal unhandled Oracle error from trying to read a row with no row source. Below 40, delete students with ID < arg4 and last name = 'OBSOLETE', then stop with the same unhandled error. Otherwise set every restaurant type with ID > 200 to arg6 + 100, then stop with the same unhandled error.

For the first three cases, don't impose row order. Count each row as soon as it's read. After processing it, if row_count >= batch_size, batch_size += 5.

After the first three cases, run final checks in this order. If status text is 'HIGH_PRIORITY', double IDs of restaurant types with ID > 100 and skip the rest. Else if the selected case was the archive case, delete restaurants with address 'ARCHIVED' and ID < threshold - 10. Else if row_count > 15, set last name = 'BULK_PROCESSED' for students with ID between arg4 and arg4 + 50 inclusive. Else set name = arg3 for restaurants with ID > threshold. Use the current threshold here, including student IDs added above.

That's it.

Return the complete stored procedure source and nothing else.

materials.text:
# How the procedure is called

It is invoked with `CALL`, never as a function, and takes its arguments by position:

```sql
CALL sp(<arg1>, <arg2>, <arg3>, <arg4>, <arg5>, <arg6>);
```

| argument | position | type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arg1 | 1 | IN NUMBER |
| arg2 | 2 | IN VARCHAR2 |
| arg3 | 3 | IN VARCHAR2 |
| arg4 | 4 | IN NUMBER |
| arg5 | 5 | IN VARCHAR2 |
| arg6 | 6 | IN NUMBER |

The names above are placeholders. Declare the parameters in this order with these types; what each one means is in the request.
